questions.title: How a secondary spermatocyte becomes a spermatid
questions.question: By which specific cellular division process does a secondary spermatocyte produce a spermatid with a haploid number of chromosomes?

explanations.A: Incorrect. The first meiotic division is what already happened to create the secondary spermatocyte from the primary spermatocyte, separating homologous chromosomes and halving the chromosome number to 23 (still duplicated).
explanations.B: Correct. Each secondary spermatocyte (23 duplicated chromosomes) completes the second meiotic division — separating sister chromatids, with no further DNA replication beforehand — to give two spermatids, each with a genuinely haploid 23 single chromosomes. The first division is reductional (halves the number); the second is equational (separates sister chromatids), and it is specifically the second division that turns a secondary spermatocyte into a spermatid.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Mitosis produces two genetically identical diploid daughter cells and plays no part in the reductional divisions of spermatogenesis.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Binary fission is a prokaryotic (bacterial) mode of cell division, not a process human germ cells use.

questions.learning_objective: State that a secondary spermatocyte becomes a spermatid via the second meiotic division.
